result.text: KX-9283 is the Wi-Fi module in the Ashby tumble dryer. It connects the dryer to the Halvard Home app.

Error E-7084 means the Vale fridge freezer’s vibration sensor detected excessive movement while the compressor was running. It may be caused by the appliance being uneven or touching nearby furniture.
KX-3107 is the voice pairing module for an Orrin heat pump.
None of the passages identify part KX-3673. The listed part numbers are KX-3639 (dryer lint filter), KX-5646 (hob cooling fan), and KX-1006 (thermostat Wi-Fi control module).
Error E-6076 means water has remained in the dishwasher’s base for more than three minutes after draining started.
The passages do not say what part KX-6507 is for. They identify KX-6505 as the replacement mounting backplate for the Lumen thermostat.
KX-3926 is the washable metal grease filter for the Fenwick cooker hood.
Error E-2194 means the Ashby tumble dryer’s factory reset was interrupted before its saved settings were cleared. Your previous preferences may still be active.

E-5107 means the mains power was interrupted while the Orrin heat pump’s compressor was running. The unit pauses to protect the compressor during restart. After power returns, leave it connected for five minutes, then press the controller’s power button once and select your usual heating setting.
The passages do not explain error E-3865. They describe E-6763, E-3946, and E-5946.
Error E-6292 means the cooker hood has detected an electrical insulation fault in its fan motor. Stop using it and switch off its power supply.
The passages do not identify part KX-3452. They list KX-7856 as a washing machine Wi‑Fi module, KX-3639 as a tumble dryer lint filter, and KX-5646 as an induction hob cooling fan.
KX-7011 is the sealing strip fitted beneath the Corra induction hob’s glass edge. It should lie flat all the way around before the hob is lowered into place.
The passages don’t explain error E-3873.
E-6736 means the Brio kettle’s lid locking clip isn’t holding the lid securely shut. If the clip is cracked or broken, the lid needs replacing.
KX-1639 is the supplied charging dock for the Mira robot vacuum.
KX-9996 is the voice connection module in an Ashby tumble dryer.

Error E-4805 means the dishwasher’s digital warranty record is missing its purchase date, so the warranty can’t be confirmed automatically. It doesn’t mean the warranty has expired. Find your proof of purchase and contact Halvard Home support with the purchase date and serial number.
On the Halvard Home Fenwick cooker hood, E-1216 means the control board cannot detect the fan motor’s speed. The hood stops the fan to prevent it running without speed monitoring.
KX-9495 is the heating relay module for the Lumen smart thermostat.

The passages don’t identify part KX-8033. They mention KX-1006 (the thermostat’s Wi‑Fi control module), KX-5646 (the hob’s replacement cooling fan), and KX-1283 (the thermostat’s replacement touch-panel assembly).
Error E-4021 means the Tessa dishwasher hasn’t drained within three minutes. A blocked drain filter is the most common cause.
KX-2446 is the drain pump fitted to the Halvard Home Keel washing machine.
Error E-3293 means the Corra induction hob’s moisture sensor has detected condensation beneath the control panel and stopped heating as a precaution.

E-7160 means the Orrin heat pump’s warranty record is missing its installation date, so it can’t confirm how much warranty remains. It’s a registration issue, not a heating fault, and doesn’t automatically mean the warranty has expired.
E-3946 means the Corra induction hob’s lid sensor has detected that the protective lid isn’t fully closed. A pan handle, food debris, or a misaligned hinge may be stopping it from closing.
The passages don’t identify part KX-5912. They mention KX-5646 for a Corra hob cooling fan, KX-3056 for a Brio kettle pairing module, and KX-7856 for a Keel washing machine Wi-Fi module.
KX-7896 is the room temperature sensor module for the Lumen smart thermostat.
The passages do not explain error code E-9454. They describe E-9544, which means the temperature sensor detected overheating during Eco mode.
KX-8645 is the removable filter for the Tessa dishwasher.
KX-5646 is the replacement cooling fan for the Corra induction hob.
The passages do not explain error E-8255. They describe Mira errors E-8250 and E-7804, and Tessa dishwasher error E-9544.
KX-3056 is the wireless pairing module for the Brio kettle. It lets the kettle connect to the Halvard Home app so you can link a supported voice assistant.

The passages do not explain error E-6779. They describe E-6763 for an Orrin heat pump and E-6067 and E-6076 for a Tessa dishwasher. Check the appliance’s manual or contact Halvard Home support for E-6779.
The passages do not identify error E-5328. They describe Lumen code KX-7896, Keel part number KX-7856, and Mira error E-7804.
The passages don’t identify part KX-1377. They list KX-5646 as a Corra hob cooling fan, KX-3107 as an Orrin heat pump voice pairing module, and KX-1006 as a Lumen thermostat Wi-Fi control module.
The Brio smart kettle supports **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi**. If your router has separate network options, choose 2.4 GHz rather than 5 GHz.
KX-1060 is the power recovery control module for a Corra induction hob.

Before leaving, run a wash, then unload the dishwasher and let the interior cool. Clean the filter according to the manual and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth.

For an extended absence, switch off the electricity and close the dishwasher’s water-supply valve. If it’s safe, leave the door slightly open so moisture can escape. If the cottage might freeze, ask a qualified installer whether the appliance should be drained. On your return, restore the supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.
E-9509 means the delay-start timer has lost its saved countdown, so the dishwasher pauses rather than starting unexpectedly.

The passages give conflicting warranty periods: P1 says **two years from purchase**, while P2 says **66 months from delivery**. Check your warranty documents or contact Halvard Home to confirm which applies.

Leave clear, appliance-specific instructions beside each machine:

- **Ashby tumble dryer:** Clean the lint filter after every load; check care labels and remove items unsuitable for tumble drying. Don’t overload it, and keep the area around it clear. Stay in the property while it runs and let the full programme, including cooling, finish. Between bookings, check the drum is empty and the filter is clean; unplug it if the home will be empty for an extended period.
- **Keel washing machine:** Check hoses for leaks or damage, turn on the water supply, and choose a suitable programme and detergent amount. Before leaving, remove laundry, check the drum, wipe the door seal, switch off the machine and water supply, and leave the door slightly open where safe. Arrange frost protection if the property may freeze.
- **Tessa dishwasher:** Before leaving, run a wash, unload it once finished and cool, clean the filter, and wipe the seals. For an extended absence, switch off electricity, close the water valve, and leave the door slightly open where safe. If freezing is possible, ask a qualified installer about draining it. On return, restore supplies and check for leaks before use.
The passages do not identify part KX-8618. They list KX-1618 as a replacement drying rack for the Ashby tumble dryer.

Frost or ice is not normal. Don’t start a programme. Switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or sharp tools to remove the ice.
The passages do not say what error E-9215 means. They cover Mira vacuum error E-7804 and Tessa dishwasher errors E-9509 and E-9544.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and securely refit the lint filter; empty and refit the water tank if your model has one. Check for clothing caught in the door and close it firmly. Reconnect the dryer and try the programme once.

If a fault code appears, note it; you can also wait five minutes while the dryer is unplugged and check accessible vents. If the warning returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support with the light or code and your model details. Don’t remove panels or attempt internal repairs. If there’s smoke or a burning smell, don’t restart it.

Set a scheduled start time on your thermostat. Choose when you want the heating to begin—for example, to delay it by an hour from 18:00, set the start time to 19:00—then choose your target temperature and save. Make sure the schedule is enabled for the correct day. Heating will only start if the room is cooler than your target temperature.

Stop cooking and switch the hob off using its controls. If it’s safe, remove the pans, then check that the control area is clean and dry and clear of anything covering it. Let hot surfaces cool before wiping them.

If the display shows **E-5238**, switch off power at the wall isolator, wipe the cool glass and controls with a dry cloth, ventilate the room, and leave the hob off for at least two hours. Don’t use a hairdryer or heater.

For another fault message, you can try switching off at a safely accessible wall isolator for 60 seconds, then restoring power. If the warning returns, leave the hob off and contact Halvard Home support. Note what flashes or appears on the display and when it happens.

Check that the extractor’s wall switch or fused spur is on, then try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole hood has lost power or only the screen. Switch it off at the electrical supply for 60 seconds, then turn it back on and try again.

If the fan and light work but the screen stays blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls still respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring; arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues.
Keep the extractor running for 10 minutes after you’ve finished cooking to help clear lingering steam and smells.

To safely relocate your clothes-drying machine:

1. Switch it off, unplug it, and let it cool completely if it has been running.
2. Remove the laundry, clean the lint filter, and empty the water tank if it has one.
3. Disconnect any drain or vent hoses, then secure the hoses and power cable so they cannot drag or catch.
4. Clear and protect the route to the new location. Use two people and a suitable appliance trolley; keep the dryer upright, and never lift it by the door or control panel.
5. Protect the cabinet and secure the dryer against movement during transport.
6. At the new location, place it on a firm, level floor and reconnect it according to its installation instructions.

For the Ashby dryer, keep it disconnected for **38 hours after moving** before switching it on. Check the appliance and connections for damage first.

Hire a qualified heat pump installer to disconnect, move and recommission your Orrin heat pump. They should handle the electrical connections, pipework and drainage; don’t move it while it’s still connected.

Stop the dryer immediately, switch it off and unplug it if you can do so safely. Don’t run another cycle or try to investigate internal parts. If there’s smoke or flame, keep the door closed, leave the property and call 999—don’t use water or move the dryer. If there are no signs of fire, leave it unplugged until completely cool, then you may clear fluff from the lint filter and check that external vents are unobstructed. Don’t use it again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.

For a Keel washing machine, finish any wash programme, empty the drum, leave the machine switched on and connect it to Wi‑Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select the machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available and follow the instructions.

For an Ashby tumble dryer, finish any drying programme, empty the drum, and leave it switched on and connected to Wi‑Fi. On the dryer’s display, open **Settings > Software update > Check for updates**, then select **Install** if an update is available.

For either appliance, don’t switch it off or unplug it during installation, and wait for confirmation that the update is complete before using it.
The Brio kettle warranty lasts for 47 months from the date it is delivered to you. It covers qualifying faults, subject to the warranty’s terms.

First make sure your Mira vacuum is online in the Halvard Home app and that you can start a clean from there. Then open your voice assistant’s app, go to the section for adding smart home devices, search for and select **Halvard Home**, and sign in with the same Halvard Home account you used to set up Mira. Allow access and ask the assistant to discover devices.

Give Mira a simple name, such as “Mira,” then try saying, “Start Mira.” If it doesn’t appear, check its internet connection, unlink Halvard Home in the assistant app, and link it again.

To safely relocate your built-in Corra induction hob:

1. **Switch it off and let the glass cool completely.** Remove cookware and loose items.
2. **Have a qualified electrician isolate and disconnect it** if it is hardwired. Don’t cut, pull or handle the fixed wiring yourself. Do not assume a dark display means it is electrically isolated.
3. **Have the installer release the hob** from its worktop fixings or seals. Don’t try to lift it while it is still secured.
4. **Use two people or suitable lifting equipment.** Support the appliance’s body as directed in the installation instructions; don’t lift it by the cable, controls or exposed glass edges. Clear the route and protect the glass from knocks. Do not tilt it more than **54 degrees**.
5. **Pack it securely**—original packaging if available, with cushioning—and keep objects off the glass. Protect the cable from crushing and secure the hob against sliding or impact.
6. **At the new location, have a qualified installer check and install it** to the instructions, including stability, ventilation, cable routing and electrical safety. Keep the ventilation openings clear and ensure the isolation switch remains accessible.
7. **Wait 17 hours after moving before switching it on.** This does not replace inspection or professional reconnection. If it was dropped, struck, exposed to water or carried beyond the stated tilt limit, leave it disconnected and have it checked.

Send Halvard Home support your hob’s full model details, a clear photo of the part if you still have it, and a short description of what you need. If the part is missing, describe its purpose instead. Ask them to confirm it’s compatible with your exact model.

Warm, moist cooking air can condense on the hood’s cold surfaces, especially in winter or when the extraction duct runs through an unheated space. Use the hood while cooking and leave it running for 10 minutes afterwards. If you see frost, don’t chip it or heat it directly; have a qualified installer check the duct insulation and outside vent.

If you’re leaving food inside, keep the fridge freezer running, set the fridge to 4°C and freezer to −18°C, and make sure both doors close fully. Remove any food that will expire before you return.

If you’re emptying it for the months away, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, wipe the interior with warm water and mild detergent, and dry it thoroughly. Leave both doors ajar to help prevent smells and mould. When you return, let it reach its set temperatures before adding food.

Check that the thermostat is powered on and responding. Turn on Bluetooth on your phone, connect the phone to your home Wi‑Fi, and keep it close to the thermostat. In your phone’s settings, allow the Halvard Home app any requested Bluetooth, nearby-device, or local-network permissions. Then fully close and reopen the app and try adding the thermostat again.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and check for app updates. Avoid factory resetting the thermostat; contact Halvard Home support if the problem continues and tell them what you’ve tried.

Stop the programme and note the exact code. Switch the washer off and unplug it for five minutes, then reconnect it. Check that the door is fully closed and no clothing is caught in the seal; don’t force it open if water remains inside. If the code returns, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support, telling them the code and when it appeared.

Provide the full model details from the extractor’s rating label and the name or description of the part you need. If you’re unsure what it’s called, send a clear photo of the existing part; if it’s missing, describe what it does. Ask support to confirm compatibility, availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before ordering.

Warm, moist air may be getting into the fridge, often because the door is opened frequently, food is uncovered, or the door seal is dirty or not sealing properly. Check that nothing blocks the door, clean and dry the seals, cover food, and keep the air vents clear. Set the fridge to 4°C and the freezer to −18°C. If thick ice keeps returning, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch on the child lock by pressing and holding the vacuum’s power button for 3 seconds while it is on and stationary. A sound confirms the lock is active. This locks the buttons on the vacuum, but scheduled cleaning and app controls remain available, so it may still start automatically. Keep your toddler away while it is moving.

To prepare your Keel washer for a move:

1. Switch it off at the socket, unplug it with dry hands, and turn off the water supply.
2. Disconnect the hoses as instructed, catch any remaining water with a towel and shallow tray, and drain the machine using the user manual.
3. Empty and dry the drum, then secure the hoses and cable so they won’t trail, swing loose or get trapped.
4. Refit the original transit bolts as directed by the manual. If they’re missing, contact Halvard Home before moving it.
5. Plan a clear route. Keep the washer upright, use two people, and don’t lift or pull it by the door, controls, hoses or cable. Don’t carry it alone.

At the new home, leave it upright and unplugged for 44 hours before switching it on. Remove the transit bolts before running a wash.

Yes. Resetting your Lumen thermostat or Orrin heat pump removes saved schedules and personal temperature settings; the thermostat reset also erases saved Wi‑Fi details. You’ll need to set them up again afterward.

Have a qualified heat-pump installer disconnect the unit and safely recover its refrigerant—don’t cut pipes, open the circuit, or dismantle it yourself. Ask your replacement installer about removal and recycling, or contact your local council to find a service that accepts heat pumps. Check collection arrangements before moving the unit; keep it upright and away from children while you wait, and use a licensed waste carrier if arranging transport yourself.

To return your Mira robot vacuum to its original setup:

1. Place it on its plugged-in charging dock.
2. Hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds.
3. Release them when you hear the reset announcement.
4. Leave the vacuum on the dock while it restarts.

Then add it again in the Halvard Home app, reconnect it to Wi-Fi, and set up new maps or cleaning schedules. The factory reset removes saved Wi-Fi details, schedules, and maps.

Check the power supply first: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. You can test the socket with a lamp you know works. If the socket works, unplug the dryer briefly, reconnect it, close the door firmly and try again. Don’t use it if the plug or cable is damaged, hot or smells burnt.
First, check that the cooker hood’s power supply is on. Check its wall switch or fused connection switch, and—if you can reach it safely—make sure its plug is fully inserted.

Try setting your daytime temperature to about **19°C**, then adjust it for comfort—lowering your usual setting by 1°C may reduce energy use if everyone stays warm enough. Use a schedule that matches your routine, with lower temperatures when you’re out or asleep; for a heat pump, try a small overnight reduction rather than switching it off.

Keep the heating schedule updated, and return to it after any temporary override. Don’t turn the temperature up sharply to heat a room faster. If your heat pump has weather compensation, ask your installer to check it if rooms are too warm or cold. Keep hot-water hygiene settings unchanged.

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your Keel washer’s model details and a description of the part. Send a clear photo of the identification label and, if you have one, the original part. Say that you need an additional item, and ask support to confirm it fits your exact model, its availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before you order.

Switch the cleaner off and remove it from its charging dock. Check the cover’s edge, hinges and catch for dust, hair or objects, and wipe accessible areas with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated properly and nothing sticks up above it, then lower the cover gently—don’t force it. If it still won’t stay down or a hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the cleaner and contact Halvard Home support.
Your Vale refrigerator needs a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**.

Unplug the teapot and let it cool completely, then empty it. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following its instructions for the amount, water temperature, and treatment time. Don’t exceed the maximum fill mark or mix cleaning products.

When finished, empty and rinse the teapot thoroughly with fresh water. Fill it with fresh water, boil, and discard the water; repeat this once before making a drink. Keep the base, plug, and exterior dry, and never immerse the teapot in water.

Move food, bottles and packaging away from the front of the shelves, push drawers fully in, and make sure the shelves are seated correctly. Clean the door seal and the surface it touches with a soft cloth and warm water, then dry them. Check for ice blocking the door, but don’t chip it with a sharp tool or force the door shut. If it still hangs unevenly or the seal is split, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the tea maker, then let it cool completely. Lift it off its base and dry the outside. Check whether water ran down from the spout or lid, and make sure it wasn’t filled above the MAX mark. If water is escaping from the bottom or the puddle keeps returning, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. Don’t immerse the electrical base or try to repair it yourself.

Start by checking the controller’s power supply. If it has a clearly labelled wall switch, make sure it’s on; if it’s already on, switch it off, wait 30 seconds, then turn it back on. If the display may simply be asleep, tap it once. Don’t remove the cover or touch any wiring.

For your Tessa dishwasher, connect it to your home Wi‑Fi, make sure no wash programme is running, empty it and leave it switched on. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected until the display confirms the update is complete.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry—never touch a wet plug or socket. When it’s safe, wipe up the water and check visible inlet hose connections, the drain hose, and whether water is running from the detergent drawer. Don’t run another cycle or move the machine while the leak is unexplained. If the hoses seem secure or water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then restart the programme—do not force the door open.

Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, all four feet are touching the floor, and it does not rock when gently pushed. If it was newly installed, check that the transit bolts were removed. If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.
Orrin heat pumps warm homes gradually and typically use lower-temperature heating water than boilers. As a result, radiators may feel cooler to the touch; that alone doesn’t mean there’s a fault.
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi‑Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.

Before first use:

1. Read the supplied installation instructions and confirm the location meets the required clearance.
2. Check the appliance for damage. If the casing, door, plug or cable is damaged, keep it disconnected and contact the retailer or Halvard Home.
3. Choose a dry, ventilated indoor location, away from open flames and at least **113 cm from a gas hob or open flame**. Keep ventilation openings clear and ensure the floor is firm and level.
4. Position it within **297 cm of a suitable, accessible earthed wall socket**. Plug it directly into the socket—do not use an extension lead or adaptor.
5. Remove all packaging from inside and around the drum. Level the dryer using its feet so it stands steadily without rocking.
6. Connect any vent hose or drainage as described in the supplied instructions, ensuring connections are not crushed, twisted or trapped.
7. Wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth.

If the electrical supply or installation is unclear, don’t connect the dryer; seek qualified help or contact Halvard Home.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Dry the tank and the vacuum’s underside with a cloth. Don’t rinse the vacuum body or put it back on the dock while it’s wet.

If the tank is cracked or water leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi, then try these steps:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone settings.
3. Turn your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the heat pump again.
5. Check your app store for an app update.

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Yes. During defrosting, ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains beneath the unit, so a puddle can be normal. Monitor it to see whether it stops. If water runs continuously or you can’t safely identify its source, contact Halvard Home support for an inspection.
No. The Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting; you must switch it on manually when you’re ready to boil water.
Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing sound while the kettle heats is usually normal.

Make sure the washing machine is on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network** (5 GHz won’t work), turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app to access nearby devices. Close and reopen the app, then follow its pairing instructions to add the machine.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and try again once Wi-Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and where setup gets stuck.

A rattling, thumping or scraping noise may be caused by loose items in the drum, metal zips or buttons, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture. It may also be unstable on an uneven floor.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, then let the drum cool before checking for loose objects and redistributing the laundry. Make sure the dryer stands firmly on a level floor and is not touching a wall or cupboard. Don’t reach underneath or remove panels.

If the noise continues, or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and securely refit the fluff filter, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and check that clothing isn’t trapped in the door. Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the light continues flashing, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support, noting which light flashes and when.

Switch the dryer off at the socket before unplugging it. Use a torch to check the area. If it’s safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry—it may be hot—and spread it out so heat can escape. Once the power supply is stable, plug the dryer back in, check the laundry and restart a suitable programme if it needs further drying. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave it unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the machine. If it has recently run a hot wash, let the water cool completely. Open the lower-front filter flap, place towels and a shallow tray underneath, and loosen the filter slowly so trapped water can drain. Remove debris, rinse the filter, wipe the opening, then refit the filter securely without forcing it.

Close the flap, reconnect the power and run a short rinse or drain cycle to check for leaks. If it still drains slowly or leaks, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. Check that food packaging isn’t obstructing the doors, and clean the seals with a soft, damp cloth. If you can see the drain hole, gently remove loose debris around it—don’t use sharp objects or remove panels.

Switch the appliance off and unplug it before checking, but only if the plug and area around it are dry. If they’re wet, isolate power at the fuse box. If the leak returns after you restart the appliance, contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi, not a guest network. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the dishwasher.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow any nearby-device or location permissions the app requests.
3. Close the app completely, reopen it, and try adding the dishwasher again.
4. If it still isn’t found, switch the dishwasher off at the mains for 30 seconds, then turn it back on and try again.

If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you’ve tried.
Recycle your old Halvard Home Corra induction hob as electrical equipment; do not put it in your household rubbish bin.

Make sure the Brio kettle isn’t heating. Press and hold the lock button for three seconds to switch the child lock on; the indicator will light up. To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds until the indicator goes out.

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects in the drum, an uneven load, or a machine that isn’t level. If the machine was recently installed, its transit bolts may not have been removed.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop and the door to unlock—don’t force it open. Spread heavy items evenly around the drum and check for coins, keys, or other loose objects. Gently press a corner to see whether the machine rocks. If it does, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting the feet. For a new installation, check the installation guide about the transit bolts.

Stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support if you hear grinding or notice a burning smell or leaking water.

Make sure the heat pump is on and showing no warning. On the controller, open **Settings > System > Factory reset**, then choose **Confirm**. Keep the power connected while the controller restarts.

A factory reset removes saved heating schedules and temperature preferences, so note them down beforehand. When the home screen returns, check the date and time and re-enter your preferred settings. If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller does not restart, contact Halvard Home support.

Connect the fridge freezer to your home Wi-Fi and ensure it has a steady power supply. On its control panel, open **Settings** → **Software update** → **Check for updates**, then follow the on-screen instructions if an update is available.

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it during installation. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm the update is complete. If it fails, check your Wi-Fi connection before trying again.

First, make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down—do not reset it while it is heating. Then:

1. Place the kettle securely on its base.
2. Plug the base into a wall socket and switch the socket on.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice; this confirms the reset is complete.

If the light does not flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly and repeat the steps.

For condensation, wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may mean there’s a leak.

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it with dry hands only if the plug and socket are dry. Let the machine and room warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a portable heater. Once thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or you find damaged hoses, contact Halvard Home support before using it again.
